title: Route external calls through one bounded-retry wrapper, with a guard tes
summary: Extend the existing 5xx retry in crates/athena-core/src/gh.rs (job 86p4) into the single wrapper: add jitter, timeout and connection-reset classification, and a per-retry log line with command and status. Add a source-scanning test that fails when `Command::new("gh")` or an HTTP client appears outside the wrapper, and tests that inject a one-off and a persistent 500 into each GitHub-calling command, including `land --pr`.

defaults_applied.how: All code and tests are Rust.
New unit and integration tests; cargo test and clippy must pass.
Extend the existing retry; use a maintained crate for jitter only if needed.
One wrapper plus a guard test, not per-call patches.
The guard is an enforced test.
One focused change, centred on gh.rs.
Behavior is checked by running cargo test.
BRIEF.md asks for tagged releases and a changelog, so the change records itself in CHANGELOG.md.

assumptions: The audit found one GitHub call site: GhCli in crates/athena-core/src/gh.rs, the only Command::new("gh"). I grepped for reqwest, ureq and curl in crates/ and found no HTTP client. The only curl is in xtask (tool download, which already passes --retry 3).
Other external processes (git, the claude agent binary) are not 'external services' for this task. The claude binary's busy-retry in athena-agent stays as it is.
The guard is a test (a source scan) rather than a clippy lint, because disallowed-methods cannot ban Command::new("gh") by argument. No clippy config changes.

Jitter is deterministic-injectable (a sleeper or jitter seam) so tests do not really sleep. No new crate is added if a small hash- or time-based jitter suffices; otherwise add the rand crate, per buy-first.
Retry logging goes to stderr via the existing output path. Each line names the command (the REST path or operation) and the status.
Non-HTTP transient failures (timeouts, connection resets) are detected from gh's stderr text, since gh gives no status for them.

acceptance_criteria.text: Retry lives in one place in crates/athena-core/src/gh.rs, built on the existing Retry and is_transient code with no second retry loop. It makes at most 3 attempts with exponential backoff plus jitter.
Transient means HTTP 5xx, timeouts and connection resets. 4xx and auth errors (401/403, 'not logged in') fail on the first attempt with no retry.
Each retry writes a log line containing the command name, the status or failure kind, and the attempt number.
Run `cargo test`. A source-scan test passes on the tree and fails when a fixture file outside the wrapper contains Command::new("gh") or an HTTP client call.

Run `cargo test`. For `land --pr` and each other GitHub-calling command (default branch, PR create/read, merged-commit and similar), a test that injects one 500 sees a retry followed by success. A test that injects persistent 500s sees a failure after 3 attempts with an error naming the command and status.
Run `cargo test`. Unit tests show a 404 and an auth failure are not retried, and that timeouts and connection resets are retried.
`cargo clippy` reports no warnings and `cargo fmt --check` passes.

out_of_scope: Retry for git, the claude agent binary or xtask downloads.
Changing the landing logic or the HostError record schema.
Changes to CI workflows, clippy config or other governance files.
departures: The change touches retry classification, jitter, logging, a source-scan guard and tests across several commands. That is larger than the typical job, so cost and time are somewhat above the reference, and pass probability is somewhat lower.
